answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by anchoring each identity to a licensed street kiosk: one real cart per agent, registered to a distinct address, with a health permit and logged sales. A trellis of neighbors cross-checks the cart's daily activity, and a rotating cipher on each receipt proves the operator was present, so a distant nebula of fakes cannot staff it. One person cannot run two carts at once, and the license fee in outside money doubles per further cart on the same funding trail, so every extra fake costs another cart, another permit, another human, and twice the prior fee.
